candidates.review_text: GREAT spot! Came here for our first anniversary dinner and truly enjoyed every part of our meal. We decided to do the chef's tasting menu and every single dish was delish.  We had heard so much about this restaurant and could not decide what to order and figured this would be a great way to get a taste of the menu in general. Our meal started off with us being served complimentary glasses of a sparkling white wine and we were told about the history of that particular beverage as it was being served. Each of our dishes was served by a different individual which was different from other places we have been. We still had one main server throughout the night as well, and she was excellent. I am always impressed when a server can tell us about various menu items without having to think about it or read the menu itself, and our server was very knowledgeable about every dish. The ambiance of the restaurant, both indoors and out, is beautiful.  It was too cold to sit outside but the garden area really is stunning at night and would be perfect for a summer evening. The overall experience was outstanding and perfect for a cozy, romantic anniversary dinner!

My partner and I went to Panorama for a little restaurant week date night, and we had a lovely time.

I really liked the flexibility of their restaurant week menu options - you had basically access to their entire regular menu and could get a smaller portion of pasta instead of the appetizer options as your First Course.  It definitely was well worth it.

I had the gnocchi and arancini and we also tried the wine flight.  The gnocchi was the softest, most pillowy gnocchi I've ever had, and I'd go so far as to say probably the best I've ever had as well.  Please note my really sad, out of focus picture does not do the dish justice yikes.

Our server was really helpful in helping us decide which flight to do.  Panorama has (being that it's a wine bar) a really extensive wine list, so for wine lovers, this is a must!  Dessert was a chocolate torte with cherry.

It's a really romantic location for date night, the interior gives off a fancy flair and vibe.  Service was great, and we left the night really feeling good about our restaurant week choice.

Tasty farm to table in a super romantic setting... what more could a girl ask for on date night?! This is totally my new fave!

Yummy cocktails? Check. Amazing service? Check. Inventive, delicious fare? Check. Romantic, rustic, candle-lit ambiance? Check.

Romantic, special place. The food is fantastic and the service is the best I have ever experienced. The outdoor patio area is gorgeous, especially at night. 
I highly recommend it for a nice date night out.

Great place to dine. Both the chef tasting and at the tables. Romantic atmosphere for date night. We look forward to going back so many nice dishes to try and can't do them all in one sitting. Service was great and we were not rushed.

Absolutely wonderful dinner
LOVES:
-great wine selection
-amazing service
-loved the branzino as well as the butternut squash ravioli!
-gorgeous ambience

MEH
-the bread basket was tiny (2 pieces for 2 people)
-parking can be tricky

Overall a great pick for date night with good service, food, and a romantic ambience.
The ambiance here is so intimate and romantic! Perfect place for date night and not too loud. The service was great! Our waiter was so attentive and we will definitely be returning!!!
The ambience was phenomenal, the food was great the service was exquisite. If your looking for a place to have a romantic dinner this is the place.

Perfect Date Night Restaurant!

The place is gorgeous once you step in, You are immediately greeted by a dazzling display of Christmas lights on the outside, making the night get off to a great start. In the summer I bet that the garden would have a just as amazing vibe.

The place indoors is very intimate and a great spot for a date. The decor is really neat and helps the vibe a lot. High ceilings, and its almost like the building used to be a bank or something.

The menu is small, but everything on it is special. I found 4 things I really wanted to try, so I got plenty of reasons to go back. 
The waiter, hosts, and bus boys were all very helpful. Each helped us at various points in the night. 

I can not say enough that the food was amazing. I ordered 'Pork & Apples'     
maple-mustard glazed pork belly, miso apple, smoky bacon, cabbage, fresh honeycrisp and pecan salad...And I have never had pork so delicious! My girlfriend had Beef & Broccoli    
sliced butcher's filet, charred broccoli, miso pickled red onion, Szechuan soubise and gingered beef jus, which was almost as good. 

I casually mentioned at the beginning of the night that it was my girlfriends birthday, and later on they brought out this carrot cake with Happy Birthday written on the plate in syrup. What a way to make her feel special!

Bathrooms are co-ed, but they are all stalls. Plenty of street parking when we went, but I can see it being busy on a week night.

Our new fav place in Philly, we will be back!

The decor and  view from this restaurant is absolutely gorgeous... A definite hot spot for a romantic dinner.

Food was cooked to perfection, service was exceptional - very courteous and prompt. I'll definitely be coming back!

Went here for our Anniversary. When we arrived we were greeted with rose pedals and a romantic atmosphere. The service and food was excellent. The steak and lobster were like butter. The sides were huge. The sweet potato casserole was AWESOME!!!! I would highly recommend this to anyone who is looking to have a romantic night out. It's expensive, but worth the price.
I had the most wonderful, romantic dinner here on a date.  Service was excellent, food was excellent, and I loved the decor.  I would certainly come back again.

This restaurant is a real cozy space (limited seating.) It is a great spot for a date night.

They have very unique plate offerings & upscale plating/presentation.

Their menu has creative food pairings. It is a bit limited but solid options for vegetarians. You can't pass up on desserts! (Rice pudding & apple cake are top notch)

Talk about ROMANTIC. I found this place for anniversary dinner for my boyfriend and I. And the second we stepped into the restaurant we were encompassed by such a romantic environment that was quiet and intimate. We started with a drink at the bar and it was delicious I had a Honey Bee cocktail. We sat down and wanted to have a cheese board and our waitress was amazing. She helped us choose cheeses for our rare preference and customize a cheese board to our liking that was divine. Next came our entree, the duck, which was also great. For our anniversary they gave us a free dessert with candles. I loved this place so much. Unfortunately my boyfriend was not feeling week earlier in the day so we didn't stay longer to eat more because he needed to rest but I would actually love to go there again and give the food a go one more time!

What a little gem of a spot! If you're looking for somewhere intimate yet low key, this is the spot. With only around 20 seats, this BYOB kills it with the seafood and gives you a cozy setting with an open kitchen. Service was great, understated yet attentive. Perfect for a date or catching up with a friend.

Been here a couple of times for a nice romantic dinner. Great menu and great drinks both times. Nice decoration, and the food is always fresh, new, and fantastic. A new twist on old styles and also manages to feel cozy and private even though the dining area is relatively large.

The best dining experience I've ever had! The singing wait staff was incredible, I had chills. The food and service was also exceptional. I recommend going to get a drink at the lounge area upstairs either before or after dinner - such a cute space. Made for a memorable, romantic date night.

Had such a wonderful dinner with the boyfriend ! Food was great , drinks were phenomenal, and loved the beautiful atmosphere! Everyone was courteous , nice and helpful! This is the spot for a romantic dinner with a loved one or dinner with good friends . I can't wait to come back again !

The staff members I encountered were rude and did not seem to know how to do their jobs. The place is way too crowded and loud to have a nice dinner. Don't go there expecting to have a romantic dinner with a significant other... The two seater tables are all shoved up against the bar so that you are elbowed my bar patrons and servers the entire time and it's so loud that you can't even have a conversation. Might be a fun place for a group of friends but definitely not a good date spot.

I went to this restaurant with my boyfriend and the food was ....fine... but the service/management  seemed inexperienced. We were sitting next to a table of women who were completely behaved and nice, but things got awkward when the waitress wouldn't serve one of the women a glass of wine. Normally I wouldn't get involved but she didn't seem drunk, and the waitress took it upon herself to embarrass the woman in front of the rest of her guests at the table. Honestly, it was very awkward and the food wasn't decent enough to overlook that weird situation. Would not recommend to people wanting to go out for a fun date night or night out with friends.

I was looking forward to trying out this restaurant for quite some time now, and decided to do so for restaurant week, but was sorely disappointed. Though the interior seemed beautiful and fancy, it presents an almost uninviting vibe for date night. The two person seated tables are wide and made it quite uncomfortable since we felt so far apart from each other. When it came to the food, everything was incredibly subpar to any other Indian cuisine I have tried in Philly and elsewhere. The meal portions and overall presentation style for most dishes was underwhelming which made for a humorous irony since the table was so awkwardly large.

This place is overrated for no reason. 
My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary dinner, based off the reviews and also I thought it was a suitable atmosphere for a romantic anniversary dinner. Plus, this place has been on my "Italian places" in the city to try. 

When we arrived, the hostess was nowhere in sight to greet us, so we kind of stood awkwardly and uncomfortably around by the doorway where other people were coming in and out. I've already made reservations and requested outside seating, but when we finally got greeted by the hostess, which she came from outside in the front (odd). She told us that there's no outside seating for us but they do have a "picnic" table option, I didn't want to be too picky so I took that option anyways, but I wasn't too satisfy since we're sharing the table with another family. 

For the food. I have nothing good to say. I did not touch my swordfish nor anything that came on the dish with it. There go my dinner. (Most expensive thing on our bill). 
And for the "infamous" spaghetti dish, which I was most excited about and a very big reason why I chose this place to begin with, was such a disappointment. 

Lastly, the waiters sucked. They keep slamming the dishes. I'm trying to have a romantic dinner with my lover here, might wanna quiet down with the dishes. 

Overall unsatisfied with everything.

I had high hope on this fairly new but seems popular restaurant. So I went there on a Friday night with a friend of mine. 

At 7:30pm, It was very crowed, fortunately we made a reservation. We were seated quickly by the window. The server was friendly and nice. Each of use ordered a drink. I ordered Lychee - it's a $15 cocktail. The drink was plain and I could barely taste alcohol. For the price I pay, I would expect a fantastic cocktail. Who wouldn't? 

Then it comes to the sushi. We actually also ordered a fried rice. It's very average fried rice, like the ones you can get in Chinatown for $8. But you pay double of the price in this "fancy" restaurant. The sushi was ok. Just ok. I'm a sushi lover, and I've tried many sushi restaurants, good and bad. The sushi we had was just average. Didn't blow my mind at all.

Overall, this restaurant is over priced for the food, but I must give credit to its ambience, very modern and romantic. They also have outdoor seating. It's a good restaurant for a date night, but don't expect good food.

Long overdue review. My boyfriend and I went here for our anniversary dinner and it was really not good. We walked in and it was really beautiful inside. The old vintage artistic feel is really refreshing since most places are so modernized that they lack architectural uniqueness. We had asked to sit outside, one balcony was open, but quite crowded so we just sat indoors. We were told that they COULD NOT open the other balcony. The menu was small and nothing was really appealing. We ordered a few starter and one entree each. The only thing we ordered that was impressive were the cheeses. The rest of the dishes were overly salted and just not good. As we were eating dinner a few other customers had come in and asked for the staff to let them sit on the other balcony that was the one we had originally requested to have opened and they allowed the other customers to sit out there. Kind of irritating when we get denied, but they offered it to the other patrons. Our waitress was quite rude as well. She just didn't seem like she wanted to work there. After our disappointing meal we went to leave and the elevator wasn't working. We had to come back into the restaurant and ask the waitress if there was another way down she seemed to be reluctant to help us and made us feel like we were stupid for the elevator not working properly, meanwhile other people were also complaining of the elevator not working. We ended up having to take the service elevator. Overall terrible experience. Absolutely awful. I encourage you to go anywhere else.

Came here to celebrate my girlfriends birthday. We decided on the tasting menu - the menu looked great, the reviews are great so lets just have the chef pick out some items for us. Boy were we disappointed. Most of the items that came out were bland, and simple. At one point we were given a plate of grilled mushrooms. Did the chef want us to taste his take on mushrooms on the grill? Did they kitchen simply run out of food, and so we were sent over some mushrooms? Does Amada think a couple paying $150 for a meal would be wow'd by a plate of flaccid grilled mushrooms? 

It very well could be that had we tried the menu a la carte we would have had a better experience - but neither I nor my girlfriend were impressed or satisfied by the tasting menu. 

Also the place is very loud, and for a place serving tapas where people are likely to order many items - the tables are very small. Not an ideal place for date night.

Went here for a romantic dinner with the husband on date night, almost no seating cramped space, practically on top of everyone else, the place was so dark and Loud and crowded, after waiting over 20 mins for waitress we left, Lousy place, this was Thursday night so not even a busy weekend! went to Standard Pub had a fantastic time quiet spacious and amazing food!

My boyfriend and I went here for date night and we got lucky because we had missed our reservation due to parking but still managed to get seated. Customer service was great here. However, food was very mediocre in our opinion. We ordered the dinner for 2 special which included 2 apps, 2 entrees and 2 sides. We had the guacamole, ceviche , empanadas. Then for entrees the nachos with sweet plantain and the Cesar salad (horrible salad btw , tasted like dust) we traded it for the coconut rice (sooo much better). Needless to say food was not great especially for the price we paid, customer service was awesome. Good ambiance but probably won't return.

Awesome setting for a romantic dinner with your love one! Family style is always the way to go! HOWEVER, we attended the restaurant during Restaurant Week and the food was just okay. And for a representation of everything on the menu you would think the food would be excellent and would bring you back.. but it was sorely lacking in taste and presentation.

Highlights: Eggplant Parm, and Tomato Pie

Gorgeous layout with well-crafted food.  My party of 2 got a table without reservations on a Sunday night (in the middle of Center City Restaurant Week).

Per previous reviewers, the staff did indeed seem quite jittery.  Based on interactions we witnessed, my guess is that the chef is a bit "Hell's Kitchen"-esque.  We attempted to place our order for drinks and appetizers, but were informed that the chef prefers all the food orders to be placed together and the waitress would give us a few minutes to make our entree decisions.  I completely understand wanting to time our food appropriately, but why would the waitress not simply wait to put in the order for the appetizer when we were ready to order?  

The food was very delicious and beautifully served in over-priced small servings.  

Ultimately, we will not be back, even for the spicy chocolate dessert ravioli.  The nervous atmosphere made it too much of an effort to enjoy our date night and the food, although delicious, did not justify the price or the atmosphere.

The two stars are for its service and nice ambience. Friendly staff and stylish deco, but the ramen was soooo salty, tasted like instant noodle. If you are looking for really Japanese ramen, this is the wrong place to go. If you are looking for friends hanging out or a date night, doesn't hurt to give it a try. Won't go back!

I was really excited to try this place out after reading reviews/watching Chef Garces on Iron Chef. I decided have my anniversary dinner here, and was disappointed :(

Positives:
- Decor was cozy-chic with romantic lighting.
- Sangria was decent (nothing special)

Negatives:
- I liked the idea of having just a few tables in the main dining area to create an intimate feel, but damn-- those tables were so close together. I wouldn't mind normally if the people I am seated next to are chill. However, on this particular night, I was seated next to this EXTREMELY OBNOXIOUS woman on a date with some guy that clearly did not care to be there. She talked on and on and honestly, never took a break. She was like Kelly from 'the office' but not in a hilarious way. 
- The food was SALTY!! I got chicken croquettes and couldnt taste anything but salt. I think the problem was that they used manchego cheese on EVERYTHING, which made every dish taste the same. We had to send back the calamari noodle/scallop dish because it was so narsty.
- The goat cheese stuffed lamb chops = overpowering. I love goat cheese, but they seriously stuffed that poor lamb chop with a whole friggin log.

All in all, Amada = FAIL

I came here in May with my boyfriend for a romantic dinner, and we had planned to do this for a while so we were quite disappointed.

The only good thing I could say here is the atmosphere.  It is amazing and the interior architecture is really something.

Maybe it's because we came 30 minutes before the kitchen was closing, or maybe their steaks always tastes much too over-sauced, salty, overcooked, and dry.  I got the filet mignon and I was very disappointed.  We also got a side of the broccoli and it was disgustingly greasy and garlic-y.

Although I had the pinot noir, I am not an avid wine drinker and cannot review the taste of it.  

To top it off, the service was something I did NOT expect at a high end restaurant.  We had to get up from our seat to find our waiter on 3 different occasions to ask her for water, the check, and to correct something on the check.
There was only about 2 other tables and a few people at the bar at this time of the night, so the waitress had no excuse for such lazy and inattentive service.  Moreover, we were late for a late night obligation, and made that very clear when we had to get up from our seat to ask for the check.  
When we DID finally get the check, she put in 2 more drinks on there than we had ordered, and we had to again, go up to her to ask her to take it off.
We finally got the revised check, and saw that the drinks she had taken off were the ones we did not get--and much more expensive.
However, judging by how late we were already, we just paid the amount on the bill and left the restaurant, disappointed with our long awaited romantic dinner.

Perhaps it was the timing of the place that could be blamed for the sub par food.  However, I don't believe that a steakhouse of this caliber should ever give such lousy service.

I used to love coming here for date night, but now it feels like they overbook shows and understaff for service. I came in here tonight with my husband and we got seated at a small shared table with another couple, with not enough space for food and drinks so that I had to hold my drink on my lap the whole time. On top of that, it felt like we were intruding on the other couple's date because I was sitting closer to them than my husband.  When we asked to be moved to another table, we were told that they were sold out and didn't have any other tables available (even though there were many visible since we arrived early). They also did not have nearly enough staff; we were seated for 30 minutes before anyone approached us for food or drink orders (and it was only because I had to get up and flag someone over), which was ridiculous. I don't think I would come back here in the near future.

The hostesses were completely unprofessional and had clearly overbooked.

The service was okay once we were seated. The mushroom polenta was good, but the filet mignon was average and their agnolotti was lacking compared to other Italian restaurants. The drinks were watered down. 

I wouldn't recommend this restaurant if you're looking for a classy date night location, the other restaurants on Rittenhouse square have better service and food.

Went here on an anniversary - service was good, but pretty aggressive - I didn't think I used a fork once before someone was there replacing it. This might sound helpful, but it was hard to have a romantic dinner without a bunch of interruptions.

Food was pretty OK - for the price, I don't think it was really worth it, and frankly, I don't think we will be back any time soon. The place has a reputation for being very fancy, and a nice place to go, but I don't quite think that it is for me, and I would prefer to go some where a bit more casual and the food is a little more accessible.

This was my first time at Marmont. My boyfriend and I came on a tuesday night for Restaurant Week, a little bit later at night - 8:30 pm - as we saw a Fringe Festival Play beforehand.

Only Pro: The waitress was friendly and the steak and food were good. Extensive wine list.

Cons: They were missing one of the desserts off the restaurant week menu (which they only had 2 desserts offered total), but were lacking in non-feminine beer & Martini variety.

Decor was not as nice as I expected from Olde City. I usually don't dine in that area, but when I do, I expect some modern, posh decor. It looked empty, dark and a bit rundown. 

Also, this killed the evening - they had live karaoke. I usually love karaoke if its in the right atmosphere... but if its restaurant week and we are trying to have a nice chill date night out, you really should mention that somewhere on your website or on the phone that there will be live singing that night of varying talent... it would have been a dealbreaker. As it clearly is.
